research.central_kitchen_or_factory: Nothing found. I checked the official-site snippets, LinkedIn, Zomato and Swiggy listings, magicpin, Urbanly, Threads and job-related searches; none mentions a central kitchen, commissary or factory. LinkedIn only says the brand focuses on kitchen consistency and structured restaurant operations and has 300+ employees. The menu, the named marinades and gravies (Angara, Banjara, Pahadi, Changezi, Kashmiri, makhani) and the prices are identical across outlets, which is consistent with centralised production. That is an inference only. The factory described in the client brief should be shown in the mock as the client's own internal fact, not as something confirmed publicly.
research.average_order_value_estimate_inr:
These are estimates; the brand publishes no AOV.

**Delivery (Swiggy / Zomato)**
- Gross order value at menu prices, before discounts: about Rs 600-700. Use about Rs 640 in the mock.
- After restaurant-funded discounts: about Rs 500-580.
- Typical baskets at live Swiggy prices:
  - 2 shawarmas: Rs 618.
  - Signature kebab with naan plus 1 extra butter naan: about Rs 610.
  - Butter chicken plus 3 breads: about Rs 800.
  - Single shawarma: Rs 309-340.
- This sits above the platform averages of Rs 425 (Zomato) and Rs 436 (Swiggy) for Q1 FY25 (Macquarie via Business Standard), because the aggregator menu is priced 40-65% above dine-in on the hero items.
- Zomato shows 'Rs 300 for one order (approx.)' on the Pune delivery-only listings. That is a per-person figure.

**In-store (Petpooja dine-in and takeaway)**
- The menu card is far cheaper: shawarma Rs 185-220, kebabs Rs 280-390, drinks Rs 80.
- Cost for two is Rs 600 on Swiggy Dineout and Rs 700-1,000 on Zomato.
- Estimated counter or takeaway ticket: Rs 250-400.
- Estimated dine-in table bill: Rs 650-900.
- Blended in-store AOV: about Rs 450-520. Use about Rs 480 in the mock.
- Confidence: medium for delivery, low-to-medium for in-store.
brand_notes: Brand story (official site, read through search snippets): Junaid started in Nashik in 2011 in a 200 sq ft restaurant in a parking lot, which grew to the 2,300 sq ft Al Arabian Express. Miya Kebabs launched in 2021 under that parent. It expanded to Bandra Pali Hill, Kalyan, Andheri, Fort, Koregaon Park and Baner.

LinkedIn describes it as 'a growing Indian QSR brand' with '6 outlets across Mumbai and Pune: Bandra, Andheri, Fort, Kalyan, Koregaon Park and Baner' and '300+ employees' (size band 201-500). No founder, funding or franchise details are public.

miyakebabs.in did not resolve (DNS failure) from my environment on 18 Sep 2026, so all official-site content came from search-engine snippets. LinkedIn lists the website as miyakebabs.com, which is a parked GoDaddy domain.

The brief mentions rolls and biryani. The current Swiggy and Zomato menus have no biryani and no rolls section. Rice is tawa pulao and bhuna pulao only. Urbanly describes the Pune menu as kebabs, tandoori, a few gravies and naan. Rolls (Butter Chicken Roll about Rs 290, Mutton Roll about Rs 360, Baida Roti) appear only on magicpin and an older menu card from about 2021-22. For the ~10 mock dishes, pick from shawarma, signature and classic kebabs, seekh, gravy, hummus and za'atar, pulao, breads, kunafa and drinks.
The dine-in menu card is chain-wide: Zomato serves the same five image files for Pali Hill and Fort. The card is undated, but Fort is a recent outlet, so treat it as current.
Delivery prices are far higher than dine-in. Swiggy prices are identical at Andheri and Fort.
Hero items carry a 40-67% markup on Swiggy over the dine-in card: shawarma Rs 185 to Rs 309, Angara kebab Rs 290 to Rs 465, butter chicken Rs 390 to Rs 599, chicken seekh Rs 280 to Rs 410.
Low-ticket items carry about 5-25%: butter naan Rs 65 to Rs 70, bhuna pulao Rs 320 to Rs 360, tangdi kulfi Rs 350 to Rs 399.
This is well above the usual 10-25% aggregator markup. The mock should therefore keep separate price lists per channel.

Zomato's website no longer shows item prices; ordering and prices are app-only. Zomato listing prices could not be verified, so the Swiggy price is used as the aggregator price. I assume it is the same on Zomato but did not confirm this.

Discounting visible on Swiggy on 18 Sep 2026: 'Extra Rs 20 off above Rs 99', 'Items at Rs 50 on select items', and bank offers (10% up to Rs 75; flat Rs 150 off). Zomato dining at Kalyan shows 'Flat Rs 175 off' on the dining payment. Restaurant-funded discounts should be a visible line in the channel economics.
Relative delivery volume, using Zomato delivery-rating counts as a proxy: Oshiwara/Andheri 5,614, Pali Hill 4,884, Koregaon Park 3,288, Kalyan 3,240, Fort 3,202, Baner 1,738, Viman Nagar 16.

Trading hours skew to evening and late night: Andheri until 3am, Fort until 3:30am, Pali Hill from 5-6pm to 2am, Kalyan 1pm-11:45pm. Mock daypart data should peak at dinner and late night, with little or no breakfast and weak lunch.

Most-rated Swiggy items at Andheri: Chicken Changezi Tikka (445), Chicken Kashmiri Tikka (291), Angara Chicken Shawarma (245), Butter Naan (219), Mutton Seekh (142), Chicken Seekh (136), Butter Chicken Shawarma (129), Butter Chicken (92).
Swiggy's FAQ for the Andheri outlet says there are 32 vegetarian items.
Reviewers at Pali Hill report that delivery orders get priority over dine-in and that waits are long. Zomato's review highlights at Oshiwara praise portion size, value and packaging.
A different chain, Chote Miya (Hill Road Bandra; also in Nashik), appears in the same searches. It is unrelated, so do not mix the two.

red_flags: The public record shows 6 branded outlets, but the client brief says 5. The 6 are Bandra Pali Hill, Andheri/Oshiwara, Fort, Kalyan, Koregaon Park and Baner, corroborated by the Instagram bio, LinkedIn, Zomato and Swiggy. Only 4 are in the Mumbai region and 2 are in Pune. Ask the client which 5 to show. A sensible default is the 4 MMR outlets plus Koregaon Park, with Baner as an optional sixth.

Leave three listings out of the mock. Viman Nagar is a Zomato cloud-kitchen listing with 3.8 from 16 ratings and is not on the brand's own list. The Nashik 'Miya Kebabs' kiosk is an unclaimed Zomato listing at Rs 250 for two. Al Arabian Express is the Nashik parent restaurant.

Biryani is not on any current Miya Kebabs menu. I checked 5 Swiggy listings, 3 Zomato order pages and the dine-in card. Rice is tawa pulao and bhuna pulao only. A biryani SKU in the mock would be visibly wrong to the client.
Rolls exist only on the Pune delivery menus (Rs 340-409). Do not put a roll on a Mumbai outlet's sales mix.
Aggregator pricing is not chain-wide, because Kalyan has its own Swiggy price list. A mock with one 'aggregator price' column would be unrealistic; model a price per outlet and per channel.

Zomato delivery prices cannot be verified from the web. The Zomato order page lists items with no prices and says 'Online ordering is only supported on the mobile app'. Any Zomato price in the mock is an assumption (Zomato = Swiggy) and should be labelled as such internally.

Hero items are priced 40-67% higher on delivery than dine-in, for example shawarma Rs 185 dine-in against Rs 309 on Swiggy. This is real but rests on an undated dine-in card from a single source. If the card is old, the true gap is smaller, so get the current Petpooja price list from the client before the demo.

Per-item rating counts and 'Bestseller' tags come from the public Swiggy consumer page. They are fine for choosing which 10 dishes to feature. Do not present them in the mock as fields from a Swiggy partner report or API unless the channel-topic research confirms that feed exists.

Zomato and Swiggy rating counts are a weak proxy for relative outlet volume, because outlet ages differ: Pali Hill dates from 2021, Kalyan's FSSAI is a 2023 series, Andheri and Fort are 2024, Pune is 2025. Counts also mix lifetime data. Use them only for rank order (Andheri > Bandra > KP = Kalyan = Fort > Baner), not for ratios.

Outlets trade past midnight: Pali Hill to 3:45am, Fort to 3:30am, Andheri to 3am. Dashboards must use a business-day cut-off of about 4-5am. Aggregator payout reports use calendar-day and weekly cycles, so a naive Petpooja-to-aggregator daily reconciliation would show false mismatches.

Swiggy shows 'Closes 12:00 am' on all five listings, including Kalyan, which Zomato says closes at 11:45pm. This looks like a display artefact of day-slotting, so do not read it as Swiggy delivery stopping at midnight.

The official site miyakebabs.in does not resolve; I independently got ENOTFOUND on 18 Sep 2026, and miyakebabs.com returned an empty page. The founder story (Junaid, Nashik 2011, 200 sq ft to 2,300 sq ft, brand launched 2021) rests on secondary sources: the LinkedIn company post, bestmenuhub, and an IndiaMART listing naming 'Junaid Kokni' for Al Arabian Express. Keep brand-story text out of the mock, or keep it generic.
I found no public confirmation of a factory or central kitchen. Show it strictly as the client's internal entity, and do not give it a public-looking address.

Restaurant-funded and platform- or bank-funded discounts must be separate lines. Only restaurant-funded discounts reduce the outlet's net, and the visible restaurant offers are small (Rs 20 off above Rs 99; select items at Rs 50).
Do not confuse the brand with 'Chote Miya' (Hill Road, Bandra / Nashik) or the second Swiggy Nashik listing 'Miya Kebab'. Both are unrelated or unverified.
verify.internal_consistency_check:
The prices and AOV estimates add up to a plausible P&L once the corrections are applied. The commission, discount and cost percentages below are industry heuristics that I did not verify in this review, so align them with the channel-topic research.

**Delivery realisation against dine-in price**
- Per Rs 100 of listed Swiggy price: a restaurant-funded discount of about 5-12% leaves Rs 88-95.
- Aggregator commission of about 18-25% plus 18% GST on the commission takes about Rs 19-27, and the payment-gateway charge takes about Rs 2.
- Net payout is therefore about Rs 60-70 per Rs 100 listed.
- Applied to the hero items, net payout lands close to the dine-in price:

| Item | Swiggy list (Rs) | Net payout (Rs) | Dine-in (Rs) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shawarma | 309 | about 185-215 | 185 |
| Angara tikka | 465 | about 280-325 | 290 |
| Chicken seekh | 410 | about 245-285 | 280 |
| Butter chicken | 599 | about 360-420 | 390 |
| Changezi/Kashmiri tikka | 540 | about 325-380 | 390 |

- The 40-67% markup is therefore coherent: it is calibrated so that aggregator net roughly equals the in-store price, and it is not an error.
- Low-markup items are margin-dilutive on delivery. The mock can show this as an insight.
  - Butter naan: Rs 70 listed, about Rs 42-49 net, against Rs 65 dine-in.
  - Bhuna pulao: Rs 360 listed, about Rs 215-250 net, against Rs 320 dine-in.
  - Tangdi Kulfi: Rs 399 listed, about Rs 240-280 net, against Rs 350 dine-in.
  - Kheema hummus: Rs 550 listed, about Rs 330-385 net, against Rs 480 dine-in.

**Implied margins**
- With food cost at a QSR-typical 32-38% of the dine-in price, dine-in gross margin is about 62-68%.
- On delivery, food cost plus packaging (about 3-5% of listed price) comes to about 22-27% of listed price, or about 35-42% of net payout. Contribution after commission, discount and packaging is about 58-65% of net payout.
- After Mumbai rent (about 8-12% of sales), staff (about 15-22%), utilities (about 3-5%) and consumables, outlet EBITDA should be about 10-18%. High-street Pali Hill and Fort should be at the lower end, and Kalyan and Pune at the higher end.
- The factory should run as a cost centre, or at a small transfer-price margin.

**AOV**
- Delivery gross of Rs 640 is about 2 shawarmas, or 1 signature kebab plus 1-2 breads. This is consistent.
- Post-discount delivery AOV should be about Rs 560-610, not Rs 500-580. For Kalyan use about Rs 570-590 gross.
- In-store: a counter ticket of shawarma plus a drink is Rs 265-300.
- A table for two (kebab 390 + seekh 280 + 3 naan 195 + 2 drinks 160) is about Rs 1,025, which matches Zomato's Rs 1,000 for two.
- A blended in-store AOV of Rs 450-520 holds if about 60-65% of bills are counter or takeaway.

**Headcount**
- 300 staff across 6 outlets is 50 per outlet. At about Rs 20,000 average CTC that is about Rs 10 lakh per month in staff cost per outlet.
- Keeping staff cost within 20-25% of sales would require about Rs 40-50 lakh per month per outlet, or roughly 250-300 bills a day. That is feasible only for the busiest 14-hour outlets.
- For the mock, use about 25-35 staff per outlet and monthly sales of about Rs 25-45 lakh, scaled by the rating-count rank order.
- Put production and HO staff in the factory entity so that the staff-cost percentage stays in the 15-22% range.
verify.notes:
**Verification method**
- WebSearch was unavailable because the session budget was exhausted, so I checked primary pages directly on 18 Sep 2026.
- I used WebFetch where it worked, and the browser pane for Swiggy, Zomato and DuckDuckGo.
- I viewed four of the five Zomato dine-in card images myself.

**High confidence (checked on at least two independent sources)**
- The six outlets are real and currently operating, and their addresses are correct. Sources: the Zomato listings, the Swiggy listings with FSSAI numbers, the brand's Instagram bio, LinkedIn, and job ads that repeat 'six outlets ... Bandra, Andheri, Fort, Kalyan, Koregaon Park, Baner'.
- Zomato rating counts are exactly as the researcher stated: Pali Hill 4,884 delivery and 117 dining; Oshiwara 5,614 and 355; Fort 3,202 and 254; Kalyan 3,240 and 278; Koregaon Park 3,288; Baner 1,738; Viman Nagar 16.
- Every Swiggy price the researcher quoted for Andheri and Fort matched my live extraction item for item, as did the Bestseller tags and rating counts. One nit: Butter Garlic Naan at Rs 105 is on the Fort menu, not Andheri.
- The dine-in card prices I could view matched the images.
- Zomato's web order page shows no prices, and the Oshiwara and Fort Zomato menu pages serve the same dining_catalog image.

**Medium confidence**
- Dine-in prices are single-source and undated.
- Baner's dine-in status is disputed between the brand's post and Zomato.
- Pune Swiggy prices match Andheri and Fort.
- Pali Hill hours vary by source.

**Low or unverifiable**
- Zomato delivery prices.
- Bandra on Swiggy delivery.
- Any central kitchen.
- The brand story from miyakebabs.in.
- The WorkIndia salary ranges, which I saw only as search snippets.
- The Nashik listings.

Each line gives the aggregator price for the Andheri/Fort/Pune list, then the Kalyan Swiggy price where it differs, then the dine-in card price.
